newsitem.title: INDIA: SBI powers Delhi shares to 2.94 pct gain.
newsitem.headline: SBI powers Delhi shares to 2.94 pct gain.

text.p: Delhi shares surged nearly three percent, propelled by reports the Finance Ministry had cleared a plan by the State Bank of India (SBI) to issue $400 million of global depositary receipts (GDRs), brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed up 21.81 points higher, or 2.94 percent, at 764.76.
"Reports of government clearance for State Bank of India's $400 million issue pushed up share prices," said Manoj Choraria of brokerage firm Choraria Securities.
Newspapers said the Finance Ministry had approved SBI's proposed GDR issue and the cabinet was expected to take up the proposal on Thursday.
SBI shot up 18.10 rupees, or 7.1 percent, to 272.10 rupees.
"The all round recovery in share prices seems to be a technical correction which was long due," said Rakesh Bhutani of brokers Multiple Investments.
Reliance Industries climbed 9.30 rupees to 205.75 on fund buying, brokers said.
TISCO surged 7.45 rupees to 183.25, while Larsen and Toubro gained 5.95 rupees to 246.45.
TELCO quoted 27.50 rupees higher at 482.50 on institutional support, brokers said.
ITC shot up 11.20 rupees to 299.45 and Hindustan Lever rose 10 rupees to 835.
